title: Conditional Gaussian filtering by Arthurs--Kelly readout in a three-mode cluster wire
authors: B. M. Rodríguez-Lara, J. A. Mendoza-Fierro
abstract: Measurement readout programs the Gaussian operation implemented by a continuous-variable cluster wire. For the standard three-node wire, momentum homodyne readout gives an additive parity channel with finite-squeezing noise. We classify the pattern-resolved input--output covariance transformations generated by calibrated uncorrelated Arthurs--Kelly readout on one or both consumed nodes. Any finite Arthurs--Kelly position record produces a conditional Gaussian filter whose gain and residual covariance depend on the input covariance entries, rather than an input-independent additive Gaussian channel. Writing $\mathrm{A}$ for Arthurs--Kelly readout and $\mathrm{H}$ for homodyne readout, the readout pattern selects the filtered sector, with $\mathrm{AH}$ selecting position, $\mathrm{HA}$ selecting momentum, and $\mathrm{AA}$ retaining both. The hierarchy $0 < τ_{\mathrm{AA}} < \min \left\{ τ_{\mathrm{AH}}, τ_{\mathrm{HA}} \right\} < 1 = τ_{\mathrm{HH}}$ shows that finite Arthurs--Kelly position records contract the gain-transferred covariance area. Our results identify calibrated uncorrelated Arthurs--Kelly readout as a measurement-level method for covariance-sensitive Gaussian filtering inside a fixed cluster graph.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes how different measurement readouts (Arthurs-Kelly vs. homodyne) affect Gaussian filtering in a continuous-variable cluster wire. It shows that finite AK measurements implement a conditional filter whose output properties depend on the input state, distinguishing it from simple additive noise channels. This provides a rigorous tool for understanding measurement-level control in quantum information processing.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the Gaussian filtering implemented by a continuous-variable cluster wire when using Arthurs-Kelly (AK) readout, contrasting it with standard homodyne readout.
main_result: Finite AK readout generates a pattern-resolved, conditional Gaussian filter whose gain and residual covariance depend on the input state, unlike the input-independent additive channel from homodyne measurements.
method: The analysis uses the covariance-matrix formalism and the Schur complement to derive the conditional output covariance for various readout patterns (HH, AH, HA, AA).
model_or_system: The system is a three-node line graph representing a continuous-variable cluster wire, analyzed using Gaussian state descriptions and controlled-phase network calculations.
key_observables: Output-to-input symplectic-area ratio ($\eta_R$) and the gain determinant ($	au_R$).

paper_structure: The paper establishes the mathematical framework for the readout patterns, derives the conditional Gaussian filtering rules via the Schur complement, and then compares the resulting filtering properties ($\eta_R$ and $	au_R$) of the finite-AK patterns against the homodyne reference.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, quantitative understanding of how measurement choices (readout patterns) fundamentally alter the quantum information processing capabilities of continuous-variable quantum systems, which is crucial for quantum networking and measurement-based quantum computation.
